title: Fixed restriction and cartesian comparison constructions
statement: Construct the open-site overlap comparison, the comparison between cartesian pullbacks across a commuting square, and the restriction comparison beta. The cartesian comparison first cancels the inverse-site equivalence by its counit, then uses the fixed derived pullback composition along the two equal scheme composites. Its component formula is the mapped counit followed by derived transport. The exact-restriction and site overlap comparisons are obtained from their canonical module-level isomorphisms by derived localization.

source.place: Compatibility of derived pullback and open restriction; composition as in Tag 0D5S.

proof.text: Reuse the adopted-source PerfectOverlapObjectRealizationCoreComparisons through a public import. It supplies the fixed restriction, site-return and cartesian comparisons with their component API; no comparison is selected anew. The adapter retains the stage-equivalence compatibility API through its existing Sheaf module. The original construction and localization dependencies remain necessary in the source library.

Retain the four additional open-square component theorems in the Sheaf adapter. Expand the source openPullbackRestrictionIso and singleComplexOpenPullbackSquareIso and identify their identical fixed composition family to prove the inverse-component equality. Apply Mathlib Iso.hom_eq_inv directly to the two component isomorphisms, using the symmetric inverse-component equality, to prove the forward-component equality. Substitute these equations into the source beta component formulas for the final two theorems. All four proofs compile with default instance-size and transparency settings, uniformly for empty and equal opens.
